SAN DIEGO—(BUSINESS WIRE)—


Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD) today reported that oral arguments were held before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit in the appeal of the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware’s May 2025 decision upholding Acadia’s U.S. Patent No. 11,452,721 (the ‘721 patent), which covers the NUPLAZID® (pimavanserin) 34 mg capsule formulation.


“We continue to believe in the strength of our position on the NUPLAZID formulation patent, on which the Federal Circuit heard oral arguments today,” said Catherine Owen Adams, Chief Executive Officer of Acadia. “Acadia believes the district court’s decision is supported by the facts established at trial and by applicable law. The trial court decided key issues of fact after hearing detailed testimony from experts. Such factual findings should receive deference from the appeals court.”


Today’s oral argument was heard by a three-judge panel, and a decision by the Federal Circuit requires a majority of two of the three judges. While there is no set timeline for a ruling, Acadia expects a decision in the first half of 2027.


If the district court’s judgment is upheld, Acadia expects the ‘721 patent to provide protection for the NUPLAZID 34 milligram capsule formulation until February 2038. If it is not upheld, Acadia expects patent protection to extend to October 2030, based on pimavanserin’s composition of matter patent, which was previously upheld by the Federal Circuit, and associated pediatric exclusivity.


As a reminder, under the Inflation Reduction Act, Acadia expects NUPLAZID to be subject to a negotiated price taking effect in 2029.


## About NUPLAZID®


Pimavanserin is a selective serotonin inverse agonist and antagonist preferentially targeting 5-HT2A receptors. These receptors are thought to play an important role in neuropsychiatric disorders. In vitro, pimavanserin demonstrated no appreciable binding affinity for dopamine (including D2), histamine, muscarinic, or adrenergic receptors. Pimavanserin was approved for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson’s disease psychosis by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in April 2016 under the trade name NUPLAZID.


## About Acadia Pharmaceuticals


Acadia is committed to turning scientific promise into meaningful innovation that makes the difference for underserved neurological and rare disease communities around the world. Our commercial portfolio includes the first and only FDA-approved treatments for Parkinson’s disease psychosis and Rett syndrome. We are developing the next wave of therapeutic advancements with a robust and diverse pipeline that includes mid- to late-stage programs in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, along with earlier-stage programs that address other underserved patient needs. At Acadia, we’re here to be their difference.
